OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: "(?s).*\\S.*"
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: "(?s).*\\S.*"
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped;
            a leading '+' and country code are kept, otherwise country code '+61'
            is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national
            digits. The result must be a '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits; this
            E.164 value is stored and returned. For example '0412 345 678' is
            stored as '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when supplied it must
            be a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned
            lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' form.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current
            date. The stored value is returned on read.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'Franklin, George'
            initials:
              title: Initials

## Summary

I implemented the household-duplicate rejection rule for owner creation.

**Change 1 — `src/main/resources/openapi.yml`**: Added a write-only `sharesHousehold` boolean to the `OwnerFields` schema. This gives the generated `OwnerFieldsDto` a `getSharesHousehold()` accessor while keeping the flag out of responses (`writeOnly: true`). Without it, Spring's default Jackson config would silently drop the unknown field and the override could never take effect.

**Change 2 — `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`**: Before saving a new owner, it now rejects the create with **409 Conflict** when another owner already shares the same household — same `lastName` **and** same `address` — unless the request sets `sharesHousehold: true`. I added two private helpers mirroring the existing telephone-duplicate style:
- `normalizeForHousehold(...)` — trims, collapses internal whitespace runs to a single space, and lower-cases, so comparison is case-insensitive with collapsed whitespace.
- `isHouseholdInUse(lastName, address, excludeId)` — scans existing owners for a normalized match (with an `excludeId` hook consistent with `isTelephoneInUse`).

**Tests**: All three acceptance tests pass — `coreRejectsSameLastNameAndAddress` (409), `functionalityAllowsDifferentAddress` (2xx), and `functionalityAllowsWithSharesHousehold` (2xx) — and the full `mvn test` run is **BUILD SUCCESS**.
